P1● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

Which of the following is not a linear equation in two variables?

ax+by+c=0ax + by + c = 0ax+by+c=0 with a, b not both zero; each variable to the power 1 and no product of variables (Topic 1). Why it applies: we only need to look at the terms.

A linear equation already in a standard form.
The constant is 0, which is allowed.
The term xyxyxy makes it non-linear (its graph is not a straight line).
Coefficients may be decimals or fractions.

Given: four equations. Asked: the one that is not linear in two variables.

Concept used: ax+by+c=0ax + by + c = 0ax+by+c=0 with a, b not both zero; each variable to the power 1 and no product of variables (Topic 1). Why it applies: we only need to look at the terms.

  1. 1

    Option (a) is already in the form 3x−2y−7=03x - 2y - 7 = 03x−2y−7=0 — linear.

  2. 2

    Option (b) is x−4y=0x - 4y = 0x−4y=0 — linear.

  3. 3

    Option (c) has the term xyxyxy, a product of the two variables — not linear.

  4. 4

    Option (d) is 0.5x+y−1=00.5x + y - 1 = 00.5x+y−1=0 — linear (a decimal coefficient is allowed).

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (c) ✔ The term xyxyxy makes it non-linear (its graph is not a straight line).
    • (a) ✘ A linear equation already in a standard form.
    • (b) ✘ The constant is 0, which is allowed.
    • (d) ✘ Coefficients may be decimals or fractions.

  5. Check: the points (1,−2)(1, -2)(1,−2), (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1) and (4,−12)\left(4, -\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(4,−21​) all satisfy xy+2=0xy + 2 = 0xy+2=0, and they do not lie on one straight line (going from x = 1 to 2, y rises by 1; from 2 to 4, it rises by only 12\dfrac{1}{2}21​) ✔.

  6. Answer (c)

    Common trap: Rejecting (b) because it has "no constant" or (d) because of the decimal.
P2● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

The pair 2x−3y=42x - 3y = 42x−3y=4 and 6x−9y=126x - 9y = 126x−9y=12 has:

the ratio test, with both equations in the same form (Topic 3). Why it applies: the coefficients decide the number of solutions.

All three ratios are equal.
This comes from mixing forms: writing the first as 2x−3y−4=02x - 3y - 4 = 02x−3y−4=0 but taking c2=+12c_2 = +12c2​=+12 gives c1c2=−13\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = -\dfrac{1}{3}c2​c1​​=−31​.
One solution needs a1a2≠b1b2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \neq \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​.
Two straight lines never share exactly two points.

Given: a pair of equations. Asked: the number of solutions.

Concept used: the ratio test, with both equations in the same form (Topic 3). Why it applies: the coefficients decide the number of solutions.

  1. 1

    Both equations are in the form ax+by=dax + by = dax+by=d: compare 26=13\dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}62​=31​, −3−9=13\dfrac{-3}{-9} = \dfrac{1}{3}−9−3​=31​, 412=13\dfrac{4}{12} = \dfrac{1}{3}124​=31​.

  2. 2

    All three equal: coincident lines.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ All three ratios are equal.
    • (b) ✘ This comes from mixing forms: writing the first as 2x−3y−4=02x - 3y - 4 = 02x−3y−4=0 but taking c2=+12c_2 = +12c2​=+12 gives c1c2=−13\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = -\dfrac{1}{3}c2​c1​​=−31​.
    • (c) ✘ One solution needs a1a2≠b1b2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \neq \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​.
    • (d) ✘ Two straight lines never share exactly two points.

  3. Check: the second equation is 3 times the first ✔.

  4. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Mixing the forms of the two equations, which flips the sign of c1c2\dfrac{c_1}{c_2}c2​c1​​.
P3● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

Is (1,4)(1, 4)(1,4) the solution of the pair 3x+y=73x + y = 73x+y=7 and x−y=−3x - y = -3x−y=−3? Justify.

Full solution

Given: a point and a pair of equations. Asked: whether the point is the solution.

Concept used: a solution satisfies both equations (Topic 2). Why it applies: we can substitute.

  1. 1

    First equation: 3(1)+4=73(1) + 4 = 73(1)+4=7 ✔.

  2. 2

    Second equation: 1−4=−31 - 4 = -31−4=−3 ✔.

  3. 3

    The point satisfies both, and the lines intersect (31≠1−1\dfrac{3}{1} \neq \dfrac{1}{-1}13​=−11​), so it is the solution.

  4. Check: solving by elimination: adding the equations gives 4x=44x = 44x=4, x=1x = 1x=1, then y=4y = 4y=4 ✔.

  5. Answer Yes — (1,4)(1, 4)(1,4) satisfies both equations.

    Common trap: Checking only the first equation.

P4● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

The graphs of x=3x = 3x=3 and y=−2y = -2y=−2 meet at:

x=3x = 3x=3 is the vertical line through (3,0)(3, 0)(3,0); y=−2y = -2y=−2 is the horizontal line through (0,−2)(0, -2)(0,−2) (Topic 1). Why it applies: the meeting point must have x=3x = 3x=3 and y=−2y = -2y=−2.

x-coordinate 3 and y-coordinate −2-2−2.
The coordinates are swapped.
This is where x=3x = 3x=3 meets the x-axis; its y-coordinate is not −2-2−2.
A vertical and a horizontal line are perpendicular, not parallel.

Given: a vertical line and a horizontal line. Asked: where they meet.

Concept used: x=3x = 3x=3 is the vertical line through (3,0)(3, 0)(3,0); y=−2y = -2y=−2 is the horizontal line through (0,−2)(0, -2)(0,−2) (Topic 1). Why it applies: the meeting point must have x=3x = 3x=3 and y=−2y = -2y=−2.

  1. 1

    Every point of x=3x = 3x=3 has x-coordinate 3.

  2. 2

    Every point of y=−2y = -2y=−2 has y-coordinate −2-2−2.

  3. 3

    The only point with both is (3,−2)(3, -2)(3,−2).

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ x-coordinate 3 and y-coordinate −2-2−2.
    • (b) ✘ The coordinates are swapped.
    • (c) ✘ This is where x=3x = 3x=3 meets the x-axis; its y-coordinate is not −2-2−2.
    • (d) ✘ A vertical and a horizontal line are perpendicular, not parallel.

  4. Check: the multiple test: 1x+0y−3=01x + 0y - 3 = 01x+0y−3=0 and 0x+1y+2=00x + 1y + 2 = 00x+1y+2=0 — no number m turns (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0) into (0,1)(0, 1)(0,1), so the lines intersect ✔.

  5. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Reading "x=3x = 3x=3" as the point (3,0)(3, 0)(3,0) only. It is a whole line.
P5● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

Without solving, state whether the pair 5x+2y=95x + 2y = 95x+2y=9 and 10x+4y=1510x + 4y = 1510x+4y=15 is consistent or inconsistent.

Full solution

Given: a pair of equations. Asked: consistent or inconsistent.

Concept used: the ratio test (Topic 3). Why it applies: both are in the same form, with non-zero coefficients.

  1. 1

    a1a2=510=12\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}a2​a1​​=105​=21​ and b1b2=24=12\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}b2​b1​​=42​=21​.

  2. 2

    c1c2=915=35\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{9}{15} = \dfrac{3}{5}c2​c1​​=159​=53​.

  3. 3

    12=12≠35\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \neq \dfrac{3}{5}21​=21​=53​: parallel lines, no solution.

  4. Check: doubling the first gives 10x+4y=1810x + 4y = 1810x+4y=18, not 15 ✔.

  5. Answer Inconsistent.

    Common trap: Seeing equal first two ratios and answering "consistent (infinitely many)".

P6● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

Solve by substitution: x+2y=8x + 2y = 8x+2y=8 and 3x−y=33x - y = 33x−y=3.

Full solution

Given: a pair of equations. Asked: x and y, by substitution.

Concept used: the substitution routine (Topic 4). Why it applies: x has coefficient 1 in the first equation.

  1. 1

    From x+2y=8x + 2y = 8x+2y=8, subtract 2y2y2y from both sides.

    x=8−2yx = 8 - 2yx=8−2ySwipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    Substitute into 3x−y=33x - y = 33x−y=3.

    3(8−2y)−y=33(8 - 2y) - y = 33(8−2y)−y=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Expand the bracket.

    24−6y−y=324 - 6y - y = 324−6y−y=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Collect the y-terms.

    24−7y=324 - 7y = 324−7y=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Subtract 24 from both sides.

    −7y=−21-7y = -21−7y=−21Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Divide by −7-7−7.

    y=3y = 3y=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Back-substitute into x=8−2yx = 8 - 2yx=8−2y.

    x=2x = 2x=2Swipe to see the whole equation →

  8. Check: 2+6=82 + 6 = 82+6=8 ✔ and 6−3=36 - 3 = 36−3=3 ✔.

  9. Answer x=2x = 2x=2, y=3y = 3y=3

    Common trap: Writing 3×8−2y3 \times 8 - 2y3×8−2y (bracket forgotten), which gives 24−3y=324 - 3y = 324−3y=3 and y=7y = 7y=7.

P7● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

Solve by elimination: 4x−3y=64x - 3y = 64x−3y=6 and 2x+3y=122x + 3y = 122x+3y=12.

Full solution

Given: a pair with −3y-3y−3y and +3y+3y+3y. Asked: x and y.

Concept used: elimination by adding (Topic 5). Why it applies: the y-coefficients are opposite.

  1. 1

    Add the equations.

    (4x+2x)+(−3y+3y)=6+12(4x + 2x) + (-3y + 3y) = 6 + 12(4x+2x)+(−3y+3y)=6+12Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    Simplify.

    6x=186x = 186x=18Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Divide by 6.

    x=3x = 3x=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Back-substitute into 2x+3y=122x + 3y = 122x+3y=12.

    6+3y=126 + 3y = 126+3y=12Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Subtract 6 from both sides.

    3y=63y = 63y=6Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Divide by 3.

    y=2y = 2y=2Swipe to see the whole equation →

  7. Check: 12−6=612 - 6 = 612−6=6 ✔ and 6+6=126 + 6 = 126+6=12 ✔.

  8. Answer x=3x = 3x=3, y=2y = 2y=2

    Common trap: Subtracting the equations, which gives 2x−6y=−62x - 6y = -62x−6y=−6 — y does not disappear.

P8● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

A father is three times as old as his son. Ten years ago, he was five times as old as his son. With present ages f and s years, the pair of equations is:

"ten years ago" subtracts 10 from both ages (Topic 6). Why it applies: each fact compares ages at the same time.

The 5 must multiply the son's whole past age, (s−10)(s - 10)(s−10).
The roles are swapped: this makes the son three times as old as the father.
The son's age was not reduced by 10.

Given: two facts about ages. Asked: the correct pair.

Concept used: "ten years ago" subtracts 10 from both ages (Topic 6). Why it applies: each fact compares ages at the same time.

  1. 1

    Now: f=3sf = 3sf=3s.

  2. 2

    Ten years ago both ages were 10 less, and the father's was 5 times the son's: f−10=5(s−10)f - 10 = 5(s - 10)f−10=5(s−10).

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔
    • (b) ✘ The 5 must multiply the son's whole past age, (s−10)(s - 10)(s−10).
    • (c) ✘ The roles are swapped: this makes the son three times as old as the father.
    • (d) ✘ The son's age was not reduced by 10.

  3. Check: solving (a): 3s−10=5s−503s - 10 = 5s - 503s−10=5s−50, so s=20s = 20s=20, f=60f = 60f=60. Ten years ago: 50 and 10, and 50=5×1050 = 5 \times 1050=5×10 ✔.

  4. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Subtracting 10 from one person's age only.
P9● FoundationShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

At a canteen, 2 cups of tea and 3 samosas cost ₹ 85, and 3 cups of tea and 2 samosas cost ₹ 90. Find the cost of one cup of tea and of one samosa.

Full solution

Given: two bills. Asked: the cost of each item.

Concept used: the four-step routine (Topic 6), with a quick elimination: adding and subtracting the equations. Why it applies: the coefficients are "swapped", so adding gives 5t+5s5t + 5s5t+5s and subtracting gives t−st - st−s.

  1. 1

    Let one cup of tea cost ₹ t and one samosa cost ₹ s.

  2. 2

    Write the equations.

    2t+3s=85(1)2t + 3s = 85 \qquad (1)2t+3s=85(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
    3t+2s=90(2)3t + 2s = 90 \qquad (2)3t+2s=90(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Add (1) and (2).

    5t+5s=1755t + 5s = 1755t+5s=175Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Divide by 5.

    t+s=35(3)t + s = 35 \qquad (3)t+s=35(3)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Subtract (1) from (2).

    t−s=5(4)t - s = 5 \qquad (4)t−s=5(4)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Add (3) and (4).

    2t=402t = 402t=40Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Divide by 2.

    t=20t = 20t=20Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Back-substitute into (3).

    s=15s = 15s=15Swipe to see the whole equation →

  9. Check (story): 2×20+3×15=40+45=852 \times 20 + 3 \times 15 = 40 + 45 = 852×20+3×15=40+45=85 ✔; 3×20+2×15=60+30=903 \times 20 + 2 \times 15 = 60 + 30 = 903×20+2×15=60+30=90 ✔.

  10. Answer Tea ₹ 20 a cup; samosa ₹ 15 each.

    Common trap: Mixing up which item has which coefficient when forming (2) — read each bill carefully.

P10●● StandardConstruction/graph · 4 marksOriginal

Solve graphically: x+2y=6x + 2y = 6x+2y=6 and 2x−y=22x - y = 22x−y=2. Also find the area of the triangle formed by the two lines and the x-axis.
Print graph paper

Full solution

Given: two lines. Asked: the solution from a graph; the triangle's area.

Concept used: the graphical method; area =12×= \dfrac{1}{2} \times=21​× base ×\times× height (Topic 2). Why it applies: the base lies on the x-axis.

  1. 1

    Table for x+2y=6x + 2y = 6x+2y=6: (0,3)(0, 3)(0,3), (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2), (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0).

  2. 2

    Table for 2x−y=22x - y = 22x−y=2, i.e. y=2x−2y = 2x - 2y=2x−2: (0,−2)(0, -2)(0,−2), (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0), (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2).

  3. 3

    The graph: the first line falls gently from (0,3)(0, 3)(0,3) to (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0); the second rises steeply through (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0). They cross at (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2).

  4. 4

    Solution: x=2x = 2x=2, y=2y = 2y=2.

  5. 5

    Points on the x-axis: (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0) and (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0). Base =6−1=5= 6 - 1 = 5=6−1=5.

  6. 6

    Height = y-coordinate of (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2) = 2.

  7. 7

    Area.

    12×5×2=5\dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 2 = 521​×5×2=5Swipe to see the whole equation →

  8. Check: 2+4=62 + 4 = 62+4=6 ✔ and 4−2=24 - 2 = 24−2=2 ✔ for (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2); shoelace with (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0), (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0), (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2) also gives 5 ✔.

  9. Answer x=2x = 2x=2, y=2y = 2y=2; area 5 square units (vertices (2,2)(2, 2)(2,2), (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0), (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0)).

    Common trap: Using the y-intercepts 3 and −2-2−2 as the base. For the x-axis triangle, the base joins the x-intercepts.

P11●● StandardMCQ · 1 markOriginal

The area of the triangle formed by the lines y=xy = xy=x, x+y=6x + y = 6x+y=6 and the x-axis is:

vertices, base on the x-axis, perpendicular height (Topic 2). Why it applies: the triangle sits on the x-axis.

The 12\dfrac{1}{2}21​ is missing.
This uses the slanting side from (0,0)(0, 0)(0,0) to (3,3)(3, 3)(3,3), of length 323\sqrt{2}32​, as the height.
This uses the x-coordinate 3 of the meeting point as the base: 12×3×3\dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 321​×3×3.

Given: two lines and the x-axis. Asked: the area.

Concept used: vertices, base on the x-axis, perpendicular height (Topic 2). Why it applies: the triangle sits on the x-axis.

  1. 1

    Meeting point: x+x=6x + x = 6x+x=6, so x=3x = 3x=3, y=3y = 3y=3: (3,3)(3, 3)(3,3).

  2. 2

    On the x-axis: y=xy = xy=x gives (0,0)(0, 0)(0,0); x+y=6x + y = 6x+y=6 gives (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0). Base =6= 6=6.

  3. 3

    Height = 3. Area =12×6×3=9= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 3 = 9=21​×6×3=9.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔
    • (b) ✘ The 12\dfrac{1}{2}21​ is missing.
    • (c) ✘ This uses the slanting side from (0,0)(0, 0)(0,0) to (3,3)(3, 3)(3,3), of length 323\sqrt{2}32​, as the height.
    • (d) ✘ This uses the x-coordinate 3 of the meeting point as the base: 12×3×3\dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 321​×3×3.

  4. Check: the triangle with vertices (0,0)(0, 0)(0,0), (6,0)(6, 0)(6,0), (3,3)(3, 3)(3,3) has shoelace area 9 ✔.

  5. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Using a slanting side instead of the perpendicular height.
P12●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

Find the vertices and the area of the triangle formed by the lines x+y=4x + y = 4x+y=4, 2x−y=52x - y = 52x−y=5 and the y-axis.

Full solution

Given: two lines; the y-axis. Asked: vertices and area.

Concept used: meeting point + the two y-intercepts; height = x-coordinate of the meeting point (Topic 2). Why it applies: the base lies on the y-axis.

  1. 1

    Add the equations to eliminate y.

    3x=93x = 93x=9Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    Divide by 3.

    x=3x = 3x=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Back-substitute into x+y=4x + y = 4x+y=4.

    3+y=43 + y = 43+y=4Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract 3 from both sides: y=1y = 1y=1. The meeting point is (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1).

  5. 5

    On the y-axis, x=0x = 0x=0: x+y=4x + y = 4x+y=4 gives (0,4)(0, 4)(0,4); 2x−y=52x - y = 52x−y=5 gives −y=5-y = 5−y=5, that is (0,−5)(0, -5)(0,−5).

  6. 6

    Base =4−(−5)=9= 4 - (-5) = 9=4−(−5)=9; height = x-coordinate of (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1) = 3.

  7. 7

    Area.

    12×9×3=272\dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 3 = \dfrac{27}{2}21​×9×3=227​Swipe to see the whole equation →

  8. Check: (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1): 3+1=43 + 1 = 43+1=4 ✔, 6−1=56 - 1 = 56−1=5 ✔.

  9. Answer Vertices (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1), (0,4)(0, 4)(0,4), (0,−5)(0, -5)(0,−5); area 272=13.5\dfrac{27}{2} = 13.5227​=13.5 square units.

    Common trap: Taking the base as 4−5=−14 - 5 = -14−5=−1 (sign of −5-5−5 dropped). Distances are found by subtracting the coordinates: 4−(−5)=94 - (-5) = 94−(−5)=9.

P13●● StandardShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

For the pair kx+2y=3kx + 2y = 3kx+2y=3 and 3x+6y=103x + 6y = 103x+6y=10, find the value of k for which the pair has no solution. For which values of k does it have a unique solution?

Full solution

Given: a1=ka_1 = ka1​=k, b1=2b_1 = 2b1​=2, c1=−3c_1 = -3c1​=−3; a2=3a_2 = 3a2​=3, b2=6b_2 = 6b2​=6, c2=−10c_2 = -10c2​=−10. Asked: k for no solution; k for a unique solution.

Concept used: the ratio conditions (Topic 3). Why it applies: a2a_2a2​, b2b_2b2​, c2c_2c2​ are non-zero.

  1. 1

    No solution needs k3=26\dfrac{k}{3} = \dfrac{2}{6}3k​=62​.

  2. 2

    Multiply both sides by 3.

    k=1k = 1k=1Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Test the constants: c1c2=−3−10=310≠13\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{-3}{-10} = \dfrac{3}{10} \neq \dfrac{1}{3}c2​c1​​=−10−3​=103​=31​ ✔ — parallel.

  4. 4

    Unique solution needs k3≠13\dfrac{k}{3} \neq \dfrac{1}{3}3k​=31​, that is k≠1k \neq 1k=1.

  5. Check: at k=1k = 1k=1: tripling x+2y=3x + 2y = 3x+2y=3 gives 3x+6y=9≠103x + 6y = 9 \neq 103x+6y=9=10 ✔ (no solution).

  6. Answer No solution for k=1k = 1k=1; a unique solution for every k≠1k \neq 1k=1.

    Common trap: Forgetting the test in step 3. Here it passes, but it must always be shown.

P14●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

Find a and b for which the pair 4x+5y=24x + 5y = 24x+5y=2 and (2a+b)x+(a+2b)y=6(2a + b)x + (a + 2b)y = 6(2a+b)x+(a+2b)y=6 has infinitely many solutions.

Full solution

Given: a1=4a_1 = 4a1​=4, b1=5b_1 = 5b1​=5, c1=−2c_1 = -2c1​=−2; a2=2a+ba_2 = 2a + ba2​=2a+b, b2=a+2bb_2 = a + 2bb2​=a+2b, c2=−6c_2 = -6c2​=−6. Asked: a and b.

Concept used: all three ratios equal (Topic 3), then solve a pair for a and b. Why it applies: the constant ratio is a known number.

  1. 1

    c1c2=−2−6=13\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{-2}{-6} = \dfrac{1}{3}c2​c1​​=−6−2​=31​.

  2. 2

    42a+b=13\dfrac{4}{2a + b} = \dfrac{1}{3}2a+b4​=31​ gives

    2a+b=12(1)2a + b = 12 \qquad (1)2a+b=12(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    5a+2b=13\dfrac{5}{a + 2b} = \dfrac{1}{3}a+2b5​=31​ gives

    a+2b=15(2)a + 2b = 15 \qquad (2)a+2b=15(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Multiply (1) by 2.

    4a+2b=24(3)4a + 2b = 24 \qquad (3)4a+2b=24(3)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Subtract (2) from (3), term by term.

    3a=93a = 93a=9Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Divide by 3.

    a=3a = 3a=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Back-substitute into (1): 6+b=126 + b = 126+b=12.

    b=6b = 6b=6Swipe to see the whole equation →

  8. Check: with a=3a = 3a=3, b=6b = 6b=6: 2a+b=122a + b = 122a+b=12, a+2b=15a + 2b = 15a+2b=15, and 12x+15y=612x + 15y = 612x+15y=6 is 3 times 4x+5y=24x + 5y = 24x+5y=2 ✔.

  9. Answer a=3a = 3a=3, b=6b = 6b=6

    Common trap: Setting 2a+b=42a + b = 42a+b=4 and a+2b=5a + 2b = 5a+2b=5 ("the same coefficients"). That makes the ratios 1, but c1c2=13\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}c2​c1​​=31​, so the lines would be parallel.

The pair kx−4y=3kx - 4y = 3kx−4y=3 and 6x−12y=96x - 12y = 96x−12y=9 has infinitely many solutions when k is:

all three ratios equal (Topic 3). Why it applies: coincident lines.

    • (b) ✘ This turns the ratio upside down: 6k=13\dfrac{6}{k} = \dfrac{1}{3}k6​=31​.
    • (c) ✘ A sign slip: −4−12\dfrac{-4}{-12}−12−4​ is positive.

P18●● StandardShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

Use elimination to show that the pair 3x−5y=73x - 5y = 73x−5y=7 and −6x+10y=4-6x + 10y = 4−6x+10y=4 has no solution.

Full solution

Given: a pair of equations. Asked: show there is no solution.

Concept used: if both variables vanish and a false statement remains, there is no solution (Topic 5). Why it applies: doubling the first equation matches both coefficients.

  1. 1

    Multiply every term of the first equation by 2.

    6x−10y=146x - 10y = 146x−10y=14Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    Add the second equation.

  3. 3

    Simplify.

    0=180 = 180=18Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    "0=180 = 180=18" is false for every x and y, so the pair has no solution.

  5. Check: ratios 3−6=−12\dfrac{3}{-6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}−63​=−21​, −510=−12\dfrac{-5}{10} = -\dfrac{1}{2}10−5​=−21​, −7−4=74\dfrac{-7}{-4} = \dfrac{7}{4}−4−7​=47​ — parallel ✔.

P19●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

The sum of the ages of a mother and her son is 50 years. Five years ago, the mother was seven times as old as her son. Find their present ages.

Full solution

Given: sum of ages; a fact five years ago. Asked: present ages.

Concept used: the four-step routine; "five years ago" subtracts 5 from both ages (Topic 6). Why it applies: two facts, two unknowns.

  1. 1

    Let the mother's present age be m years and the son's be s years.

  2. 2

    Sum.

    m+s=50(1)m + s = 50 \qquad (1)m+s=50(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Five years ago: m−5=7(s−5)m - 5 = 7(s - 5)m−5=7(s−5). Expand the bracket.

    m−5=7s−35m - 5 = 7s - 35m−5=7s−35Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract 7s7s7s from both sides.

    m−7s−5=−35m - 7s - 5 = -35m−7s−5=−35Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Add 5 to both sides.

    m−7s=−30(2)m - 7s = -30 \qquad (2)m−7s=−30(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Subtract (2) from (1), term by term.

    (m−m)+(s+7s)=50−(−30)(m - m) + (s + 7s) = 50 - (-30)(m−m)+(s+7s)=50−(−30)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Simplify.

    8s=808s = 808s=80Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Divide by 8.

    s=10s = 10s=10Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Back-substitute into (1).

    m=40m = 40m=40Swipe to see the whole equation →

  10. Check (story): 40+10=5040 + 10 = 5040+10=50 ✔; five years ago 35 and 5, and 35=7×535 = 7 \times 535=7×5 ✔.

  11. Answer Mother 40 years, son 10 years.

    Common trap: Writing m−5=7s−5m - 5 = 7s - 5m−5=7s−5 — the 7 must multiply the whole of (s−5)(s - 5)(s−5).

P20●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 11. The number obtained by reversing its digits is 27 more than the original number. Find the number.

Full solution

Given: digit sum 11; reversed = original + 27. Asked: the number.

Concept used: number =10x+y= 10x + y=10x+y, reversed =10y+x= 10y + x=10y+x (Topic 6). Why it applies: the question compares a number with its reverse.

  1. 1

    Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y. Number =10x+y= 10x + y=10x+y; reversed =10y+x= 10y + x=10y+x.

  2. 2

    Digit sum.

    x+y=11(1)x + y = 11 \qquad (1)x+y=11(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Reversed is 27 more.

    10y+x=10x+y+2710y + x = 10x + y + 2710y+x=10x+y+27Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract x from both sides.

    10y=9x+y+2710y = 9x + y + 2710y=9x+y+27Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Subtract y from both sides.

    9y=9x+279y = 9x + 279y=9x+27Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Divide by 9.

    y=x+3(2)y = x + 3 \qquad (2)y=x+3(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Substitute (2) into (1).

    x+x+3=11x + x + 3 = 11x+x+3=11Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Collect the x-terms.

    2x+3=112x + 3 = 112x+3=11Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Subtract 3 from both sides.

    2x=82x = 82x=8Swipe to see the whole equation →
  10. 10

    Divide by 2.

    x=4x = 4x=4Swipe to see the whole equation →
  11. 11

    Back-substitute into (2).

    y=7y = 7y=7Swipe to see the whole equation →

  12. Check (story): the number is 47; 4+7=114 + 7 = 114+7=11 ✔; 74−47=2774 - 47 = 2774−47=27 ✔.

  13. Answer The number is 47.

    Common trap: Writing "27 more" the wrong way round: 10x+y=10y+x+2710x + y = 10y + x + 2710x+y=10y+x+27, which gives 74 — the reverse of the answer.

The denominator of a fraction is 4 more than its numerator. If 1 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, the fraction becomes 35\dfrac{3}{5}53​. Find the fraction.

Full solution

Given: denominator = numerator + 4; x+1y+1=35\dfrac{x + 1}{y + 1} = \dfrac{3}{5}y+1x+1​=53​. Asked: the fraction.

Concept used: let the fraction be xy\dfrac{x}{y}yx​; substitution (Topic 6). Why it applies: the first fact gives y in terms of x.

  1. 1

    Let the fraction be xy\dfrac{x}{y}yx​.

  2. 2

    First fact.

    y=x+4(1)y = x + 4 \qquad (1)y=x+4(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Second fact, cross-multiplied.

    5(x+1)=3(y+1)5(x + 1) = 3(y + 1)5(x+1)=3(y+1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Substitute (1).

    5(x+1)=3(x+5)5(x + 1) = 3(x + 5)5(x+1)=3(x+5)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Expand both brackets.

    5x+5=3x+155x + 5 = 3x + 155x+5=3x+15Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Subtract 3x3x3x from both sides.

    2x+5=152x + 5 = 152x+5=15Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Subtract 5 from both sides.

    2x=102x = 102x=10Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Divide by 2.

    x=5x = 5x=5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Back-substitute into (1).

    y=9y = 9y=9Swipe to see the whole equation →

  10. Check (story): 9=5+49 = 5 + 49=5+4 ✔ and 5+19+1=610=35\dfrac{5 + 1}{9 + 1} = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}9+15+1​=106​=53​ ✔.

  11. Answer The fraction is 59\dfrac{5}{9}95​.

    Common trap: Cross-multiplying as 3(x+1)=5(y+1)3(x + 1) = 5(y + 1)3(x+1)=5(y+1), which leads to a negative numerator.

P22●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

A mobile repair service charges a fixed visit fee plus an hourly rate. A 2-hour job costs ₹ 650 and a 5-hour job costs ₹ 1250. Find the visit fee and the hourly rate. How much does a job of 3 hours 30 minutes cost?

Full solution

Given: two jobs and their costs. Asked: the fee, the rate, and the cost of 3.5 hours.

Concept used: total = fee + rate × hours; elimination (Topic 6). Why it applies: the fee is the same in both.

  1. 1

    Let the visit fee be ₹ f and the hourly rate be ₹ r.

  2. 2

    Write the equations.

    f+2r=650(1)f + 2r = 650 \qquad (1)f+2r=650(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
    f+5r=1250(2)f + 5r = 1250 \qquad (2)f+5r=1250(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Subtract (1) from (2), term by term.

    3r=6003r = 6003r=600Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Divide by 3.

    r=200r = 200r=200Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Back-substitute into (1).

    f+400=650f + 400 = 650f+400=650Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Subtract 400 from both sides.

    f=250f = 250f=250Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    For 3 hours 30 minutes, use 3.5 hours.

    f+3.5r=250+700=950f + 3.5r = 250 + 700 = 950f+3.5r=250+700=950Swipe to see the whole equation →

  8. Check (story): 250+2×200=650250 + 2 \times 200 = 650250+2×200=650 ✔; 250+5×200=1250250 + 5 \times 200 = 1250250+5×200=1250 ✔.

  9. Answer Visit fee ₹ 250, ₹ 200 per hour; a 3 h 30 min job costs ₹ 950.

    Common trap: Using 3.30 hours for "3 hours 30 minutes". Thirty minutes is 0.5 hour, so use 3.5.

    Angle sum.

    Subtract 60 from both sides.

    3x=1203x = 1203x=120Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Divide by 3.

    x=40x = 40x=40Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    ∠A−∠B=20\angle A - \angle B = 20∠A−∠B=20.

    (x+y)−(2x−y)=20(x + y) - (2x - y) = 20(x+y)−(2x−y)=20Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Remove the brackets.

    −x+2y=20-x + 2y = 20−x+2y=20Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Substitute x=40x = 40x=40.

    −40+2y=20-40 + 2y = 20−40+2y=20Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Add 40 to both sides.

    2y=602y = 602y=60Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Divide by 2.

    y=30y = 30y=30Swipe to see the whole equation →
  10. 10

    Angles: ∠A=70°\angle A = 70°∠A=70°, ∠B=80−30=50°\angle B = 80 - 30 = 50°∠B=80−30=50°, ∠C=60°\angle C = 60°∠C=60°.

  11. Check: 70°+50°+60°=180°70° + 50° + 60° = 180°70°+50°+60°=180° ✔ and 70°−50°=20°70° - 50° = 20°70°−50°=20° ✔.

  12. Answer x=40x = 40x=40, y=30y = 30y=30; ∠A=70°\angle A = 70°∠A=70°, ∠B=50°\angle B = 50°∠B=50°, ∠C=60°\angle C = 60°∠C=60°.

P24●● StandardMCQ · 1 markOriginal

Using the "Which method?" list from Topic 5, for which pair is substitution the more convenient method?

the ordered "Which method?" list (Topic 5): use the first row that fits. Why it applies: the list gives one choice for each pair.

y is already the subject.
Adding removes y at once.
Making x or y the subject gives fractions; elimination is neater.
Subtracting removes x at once.

Given: four pairs. Asked: the pair for which substitution is the first row that fits.

Concept used: the ordered "Which method?" list (Topic 5): use the first row that fits. Why it applies: the list gives one choice for each pair.

  1. 1

    (a) Row 1 fits: one equation already says y=…y = \ldotsy=… → substitution.

  2. 2

    (b) Row 2 fits: +2y+2y+2y and −2y-2y−2y are opposite → elimination.

  3. 3

    (c) Rows 1–3 do not fit (no coefficient is 1 or −1-1−1) → row 4, elimination.

  4. 4

    (d) Row 2 fits: the x-coefficients are equal → elimination.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ y is already the subject.
    • (b) ✘ Adding removes y at once.
    • (c) ✘ Making x or y the subject gives fractions; elimination is neater.
    • (d) ✘ Subtracting removes x at once.

  5. Check: both methods always work; for (a), substitution gives 4x+5(3x−1)=74x + 5(3x - 1) = 74x+5(3x−1)=7, so 19x=1219x = 1219x=12 in one step ✔.

  6. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Thinking one of the methods "fails" for some pairs. Both always work; the list only picks the quicker one.
P25●●● AdvancedConstruction/graph · 5 marksOriginal

Draw the graphs of 2x+y=82x + y = 82x+y=8 and x−y=−2x - y = -2x−y=−2. Find the vertices of the triangle formed by these lines and (a) the x-axis (b) the y-axis. Find the ratio of the areas of the two triangles.
Print graph paper

Full solution

Given: two lines. Asked: the vertices of both triangles and the ratio of their areas.

Concept used: meeting point + axis points; height = the other coordinate of the meeting point (its distance from the axis — drop any minus sign) (Topic 2). Why it applies: each triangle has its base on an axis.

  1. 1

    Area=12×6×4=12\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12Area=21​×6×4=12Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    (b) y-axis: vertices (2,4)(2, 4)(2,4), (0,8)(0, 8)(0,8), (0,2)(0, 2)(0,2). Base =8−2=6= 8 - 2 = 6=8−2=6; height =2= 2=2.

    Area=12×6×2=6\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 2 = 6Area=21​×6×2=6Swipe to see the whole equation →

P26●●● AdvancedShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

For the pair 2x+ky=12x + ky = 12x+ky=1 and kx+8y=4kx + 8y = 4kx+8y=4, find all values of k for which the pair has (i) no solution (ii) infinitely many solutions.

Full solution

Given: a1=2a_1 = 2a1​=2, b1=kb_1 = kb1​=k, c1=−1c_1 = -1c1​=−1; a2=ka_2 = ka2​=k, b2=8b_2 = 8b2​=8, c2=−4c_2 = -4c2​=−4. Asked: k for each case.

Concept used: the ratio conditions; each candidate tested (Topic 3). Why it applies: both cases need a1a2=b1b2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​ first.

  1. 1

    2k=k8\dfrac{2}{k} = \dfrac{k}{8}k2​=8k​. Cross-multiply.

    k2=16k^2 = 16k2=16Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    So k=4k = 4k=4 or k=−4k = -4k=−4. (At k=0k = 0k=0 the ratio 20\dfrac{2}{0}02​ has no value; then the pair is 2x=12x = 12x=1 and 8y=48y = 48y=4, which meet at one point, so k=0k = 0k=0 is not a candidate.)

  3. 3

    Test k=4k = 4k=4: ratios 24=12\dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}42​=21​, 48=12\dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2}84​=21​, −1−4=14\dfrac{-1}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{4}−4−1​=41​ — parallel.

  4. 4

    Test k=−4k = -4k=−4: ratios 2−4=−12\dfrac{2}{-4} = -\dfrac{1}{2}−42​=−21​, −48=−12\dfrac{-4}{8} = -\dfrac{1}{2}8−4​=−21​, 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​ — parallel.

  5. 5

    (i) Both values give parallel lines.

  6. 6

    (ii) Infinitely many would need 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​ to equal ±12\pm\dfrac{1}{2}±21​ as well — impossible.

  7. Check: at k=4k = 4k=4: doubling 2x+4y=12x + 4y = 12x+4y=1 gives 4x+8y=2≠44x + 8y = 2 \neq 44x+8y=2=4 ✔. At k=−4k = -4k=−4: −2(2x−4y)=−4x+8y=−2≠4-2(2x - 4y) = -4x + 8y = -2 \neq 4−2(2x−4y)=−4x+8y=−2=4 ✔.

  8. Answer (i) k=4k = 4k=4 or k=−4k = -4k=−4 (ii) no value of k.

    Common trap: Keeping only k=4k = 4k=4 (forgetting the negative square root), or assuming one of the two must be rejected. Test each one.

P27●●● AdvancedCase/source-based · 4 marksOriginal

Case: the plant nursery

At a plant nursery, Rosy buys 3 rose plants and 5 tulsi plants for ₹ 410. Ali buys 4 rose plants and 2 tulsi plants for ₹ 360. Let one rose plant cost ₹ r and one tulsi plant cost ₹ t.

(i) Write the equation for Rosy's purchase. (1)
(ii) Write the equation for Ali's purchase. (1)
(iii) (A) Find the cost of one rose plant and one tulsi plant. (2)

OR
(iii) (B) How much would 2 rose plants and 3 tulsi plants cost? (2)

Full solution

Given: two purchases. Asked: as above.

Concept used: forming equations; substitution (Topic 6). Why it applies: halving Ali's equation gives t with coefficient 1.

  1. 1

    (i) Rosy's purchase.

    3r+5t=4103r + 5t = 4103r+5t=410Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    (ii) Ali's purchase.

    4r+2t=3604r + 2t = 3604r+2t=360Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    (iii) Divide Ali's equation by 2.

    2r+t=1802r + t = 1802r+t=180Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract 2r2r2r from both sides.

    t=180−2rt = 180 - 2rt=180−2rSwipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Substitute into Rosy's equation.

    3r+5(180−2r)=4103r + 5(180 - 2r) = 4103r+5(180−2r)=410Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Expand the bracket.

    3r+900−10r=4103r + 900 - 10r = 4103r+900−10r=410Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Collect the r-terms.

    900−7r=410900 - 7r = 410900−7r=410Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Subtract 900 from both sides.

    −7r=−490-7r = -490−7r=−490Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Divide by −7-7−7.

    r=70r = 70r=70Swipe to see the whole equation →
  10. 10

    Back-substitute into t=180−2rt = 180 - 2rt=180−2r.

    t=180−140=40t = 180 - 140 = 40t=180−140=40Swipe to see the whole equation →
  11. 11

    (iii)(B): 2×70+3×40=140+120=2602 \times 70 + 3 \times 40 = 140 + 120 = 2602×70+3×40=140+120=260.

  12. Check (story): Rosy: 210+200=410210 + 200 = 410210+200=410 ✔; Ali: 280+80=360280 + 80 = 360280+80=360 ✔.

  13. Answer (i) 3r+5t=4103r + 5t = 4103r+5t=410 (ii) 4r+2t=3604r + 2t = 3604r+2t=360 (iii)(A) rose plant ₹ 70, tulsi plant ₹ 40 — OR — (iii)(B) ₹ 260.

    Common trap: In (iii)(B), trying to answer without solving. The cost of 2 roses and 3 tulsi needs both prices.

P28●●● AdvancedShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

A grocer mixes two varieties of rice costing ₹ 50 per kg and ₹ 70 per kg to make 40 kg of a mixture worth ₹ 62 per kg. How many kilograms of each variety does he use?

Full solution

Given: two prices; total mass 40 kg; mixture price ₹ 62 per kg. Asked: the mass of each variety.

Concept used: total mass and total value give two equations (Topic 6). Why it applies: value = price × mass for each part.

  1. 1

    Let x kg of the ₹ 50 rice and y kg of the ₹ 70 rice be used.

  2. 2

    Total mass.

    x+y=40(1)x + y = 40 \qquad (1)x+y=40(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Total value: 40×62=248040 \times 62 = 248040×62=2480.

    50x+70y=2480(2)50x + 70y = 2480 \qquad (2)50x+70y=2480(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    From (1), y=40−xy = 40 - xy=40−x. Substitute into (2).

    50x+70(40−x)=248050x + 70(40 - x) = 248050x+70(40−x)=2480Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Expand the bracket.

    50x+2800−70x=248050x + 2800 - 70x = 248050x+2800−70x=2480Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Collect the x-terms.

    2800−20x=24802800 - 20x = 24802800−20x=2480Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Subtract 2800 from both sides.

    −20x=−320-20x = -320−20x=−320Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Divide by −20-20−20.

    x=16x = 16x=16Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Back-substitute into (1).

    y=24y = 24y=24Swipe to see the whole equation →

  10. Check (story): 16+24=4016 + 24 = 4016+24=40 kg ✔; value 16×50+24×70=800+1680=2480=40×6216 \times 50 + 24 \times 70 = 800 + 1680 = 2480 = 40 \times 6216×50+24×70=800+1680=2480=40×62 ✔.

  11. Answer 16 kg of the ₹ 50 rice and 24 kg of the ₹ 70 rice.

    Common trap: Writing the value equation as 50x+70y=6250x + 70y = 6250x+70y=62 (the price per kg instead of the total value).

P29●●● AdvancedTrue/False with justification · 2 marksOriginal

True or false? Justify: "If a pair of linear equations in two variables has two different solutions, then it has infinitely many solutions."

Full solution

Given: a pair with two different solutions. Asked: is the statement true?

Concept used: two different straight lines meet in at most one point (Topic 2). Why it applies: each solution is a point on both lines.

  1. 1

    Each solution is a point lying on both lines.

  2. 2

    Two different points lie on both lines.

  3. 3

    Through two different points there is only one straight line, so the two lines must be the same line.

  4. 4

    Coincident lines have infinitely many common points.

  5. Check: an example: x+y=2x + y = 2x+y=2 and 2x+2y=42x + 2y = 42x+2y=4 have the two solutions (0,2)(0, 2)(0,2) and (2,0)(2, 0)(2,0) — and also (1,1)(1, 1)(1,1), (3,−1)(3, -1)(3,−1), … ✔.

  6. Answer True. A pair of linear equations has 0, 1 or infinitely many solutions — never exactly two.

    Common trap: Thinking that, as with quadratic equations, two solutions are possible. Linear pairs cannot have exactly two.

Tick each part you got right:

You got 0 of 1 parts.

P30●●● AdvancedMCQ · 1 markOriginal

A pair of linear equations has its only solution at (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1). One of the equations is 3x+y=53x + y = 53x+y=5. Which of these could be the other equation?
I: 6x+2y=106x + 2y = 106x+2y=10 II: x−y=3x - y = 3x−y=3 III: x+2y=1x + 2y = 1x+2y=1

the other line must pass through (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1) and intersect 3x+y=53x + y = 53x+y=5 at one point (Topics 2–3). Why it applies: "only solution" means exactly one common point.

I gives infinitely many solutions, not "only" (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1).
Same reason as (b).
III does not pass through (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1).

Given: the only solution (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1); one equation 3x+y=53x + y = 53x+y=5. Asked: which equations could complete the pair.

Concept used: the other line must pass through (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1) and intersect 3x+y=53x + y = 53x+y=5 at one point (Topics 2–3). Why it applies: "only solution" means exactly one common point.

  1. 1

    I: 6(2)+2(−1)=106(2) + 2(-1) = 106(2)+2(−1)=10 ✔ passes through the point, but it is 2 times 3x+y=53x + y = 53x+y=5 — coincident, infinitely many solutions. Reject.

  2. 2

    II: 2−(−1)=32 - (-1) = 32−(−1)=3 ✔ passes through the point; ratios 31≠1−1\dfrac{3}{1} \neq \dfrac{1}{-1}13​=−11​ — intersecting. Accept.

  3. 3

    III: 2+2(−1)=0≠12 + 2(-1) = 0 \neq 12+2(−1)=0=1 — the point is not on it. Reject.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔
    • (b) ✘ I gives infinitely many solutions, not "only" (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1).
    • (c) ✘ Same reason as (b).
    • (d) ✘ III does not pass through (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1).

  4. Check: solving 3x+y=53x + y = 53x+y=5 and x−y=3x - y = 3x−y=3: adding gives 4x=84x = 84x=8, x=2x = 2x=2, y=−1y = -1y=−1 ✔.

  5. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Accepting I because (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1) satisfies it. It satisfies it because it is the same line.

    Multiply −5x+7y=2-5x + 7y = 2−5x+7y=2 by −2-2−2: 10x−14y=−410x - 14y = -410x−14y=−4. This is (D).

    Reasoning for each option: (D) ✔. (A), (B) ✘ the x- and y-coefficients are not in the ratio −5:7-5 : 7−5:7. (C) ✘ correct x- and y-parts, wrong sign of the constant — parallel.

  3. Check: ratios for (D): −510=−12\dfrac{-5}{10} = -\dfrac{1}{2}10−5​=−21​, 7−14=−12\dfrac{7}{-14} = -\dfrac{1}{2}−147​=−21​, 2−4=−12\dfrac{2}{-4} = -\dfrac{1}{2}−42​=−21​ ✔.

    Common trap: Choosing (C) after moving the constant without changing its sign.

E10●● StandardTrue/False with justification · 2 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 3, Ex 3.2 Q4

For the pair of equations λx+3y=−7\lambda x + 3y = -7λx+3y=−7, 2x+6y=142x + 6y = 142x+6y=14 to have infinitely many solutions, the value of λ\lambdaλ should be 1. Is the statement true? Give reasons.

Full solution

Given: a1=λa_1 = \lambdaa1​=λ, b1=3b_1 = 3b1​=3, d1=−7d_1 = -7d1​=−7; a2=2a_2 = 2a2​=2, b2=6b_2 = 6b2​=6, d2=14d_2 = 14d2​=14. Asked: is λ=1\lambda = 1λ=1 right?

Concept used: infinitely many ⇔ all three ratios equal (Topic 3). Why it applies: the b- and constant ratios are fixed.

  1. 1

    b1b2=36=12\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}b2​b1​​=63​=21​ and d1d2=−714=−12\dfrac{d_1}{d_2} = \dfrac{-7}{14} = -\dfrac{1}{2}d2​d1​​=14−7​=−21​.

  2. 2

    These are never equal, so no value of λ\lambdaλ gives infinitely many solutions.

  3. 3

    With λ=1\lambda = 1λ=1, a1a2=12=b1b2≠d1d2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \dfrac{d_1}{d_2}a2​a1​​=21​=b2​b1​​=d2​d1​​: the lines are parallel — no solution.

  4. Check: doubling x+3y=−7x + 3y = -7x+3y=−7 gives 2x+6y=−142x + 6y = -142x+6y=−14, not 14 ✔.

  5. Answer No, the statement is not true. For λ=1\lambda = 1λ=1 the pair has no solution; no value of λ\lambdaλ gives infinitely many solutions.

    Common trap: Checking only a1a2=b1b2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​.

For all real values of c, the pair of equations x−2y=8x - 2y = 8x−2y=8, 5x−10y=c5x - 10y = c5x−10y=c have a unique solution. Justify whether it is true or false.

Given: a1=1a_1 = 1a1​=1, b1=−2b_1 = -2b1​=−2; a2=5a_2 = 5a2​=5, b2=−10b_2 = -10b2​=−10. Asked: true or false.

Concept used: a unique solution needs a1a2≠b1b2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \neq \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​ (Topic 3). Why it applies: c does not affect the first two ratios.

    a1a2=15\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{1}{5}a2​a1​​=51​ and b1b2=−2−10=15\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{-2}{-10} = \dfrac{1}{5}b2​b1​​=−10−2​=51​: equal for every c.

    So the pair never has a unique solution: for c=40c = 40c=40 the lines coincide, and for every other c they are parallel.

For which value(s) of k will the pair of equations kx+3y=k−3kx + 3y = k - 3kx+3y=k−3, 12x+ky=k12x + ky = k12x+ky=k have no solution?

Full solution

Given: a1=ka_1 = ka1​=k, b1=3b_1 = 3b1​=3, d1=k−3d_1 = k - 3d1​=k−3; a2=12a_2 = 12a2​=12, b2=kb_2 = kb2​=k, d2=kd_2 = kd2​=k. Asked: k for no solution.

Concept used: no solution ⇔ a1a2=b1b2≠d1d2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \dfrac{d_1}{d_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​=d2​d1​​; test each candidate (Topic 3). Why it applies: a1a2=b1b2\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​ gives two candidates.

  1. 1

    k12=3k\dfrac{k}{12} = \dfrac{3}{k}12k​=k3​. Cross-multiply: k2=36k^2 = 36k2=36, so k=6k = 6k=6 or k=−6k = -6k=−6. (At k=0k = 0k=0: 3y=−33y = -33y=−3 and 12x=012x = 012x=0 meet at one point, so 0 is not a candidate.)

  2. 2

    Test k=6k = 6k=6: ratios 612=12\dfrac{6}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2}126​=21​, 36=12\dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}63​=21​, 36=12\dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}63​=21​ — all equal, coincident. Reject.

  3. 3

    Test k=−6k = -6k=−6: ratios −12-\dfrac{1}{2}−21​, 3−6=−12\dfrac{3}{-6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}−63​=−21​, −9−6=32\dfrac{-9}{-6} = \dfrac{3}{2}−6−9​=23​ — parallel ✔.

  4. Check: with k=−6k = -6k=−6: −6x+3y=−9-6x + 3y = -9−6x+3y=−9 and 12x−6y=−612x - 6y = -612x−6y=−6. Multiplying the first by −2-2−2 gives 12x−6y=18≠−612x - 6y = 18 \neq -612x−6y=18=−6 ✔.

E14●●● AdvancedShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 3, Ex 3.3 Q3

For which values of a and b, will the following pair of linear equations have infinitely many solutions?
x+2y=1x + 2y = 1x+2y=1
(a−b)x+(a+b)y=a+b−2(a - b)x + (a + b)y = a + b - 2(a−b)x+(a+b)y=a+b−2

Full solution

Given: a1=1a_1 = 1a1​=1, b1=2b_1 = 2b1​=2, d1=1d_1 = 1d1​=1; a2=a−ba_2 = a - ba2​=a−b, b2=a+bb_2 = a + bb2​=a+b, d2=a+b−2d_2 = a + b - 2d2​=a+b−2. Asked: a and b.

Concept used: all three ratios equal (Topic 3). Why it applies: coincident lines.

  1. 1

    2a+b=1a+b−2\dfrac{2}{a + b} = \dfrac{1}{a + b - 2}a+b2​=a+b−21​. Cross-multiply: 2(a+b)−4=a+b2(a + b) - 4 = a + b2(a+b)−4=a+b, so a+b=4a + b = 4a+b=4.

  2. 2

    1a−b=2a+b=24=12\dfrac{1}{a - b} = \dfrac{2}{a + b} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}a−b1​=a+b2​=42​=21​, so a−b=2a - b = 2a−b=2.

  3. 3

    Add the two equations: 2a=62a = 62a=6, so a=3a = 3a=3; then b=1b = 1b=1.

  4. Check: the second equation becomes 2x+4y=22x + 4y = 22x+4y=2, which is 2×(x+2y=1)2 \times (x + 2y = 1)2×(x+2y=1) ✔.

  5. Answer a=3a = 3a=3, b=1b = 1b=1

    Common trap: Using only two of the three ratios — that gives one equation in a and b, not two.

E17●●● AdvancedShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 3, Ex 3.4 Q9

A two-digit number is obtained by either multiplying the sum of the digits by 8 and then subtracting 5 or by multiplying the difference of the digits by 16 and then adding 3. Find the number.

Full solution

Given: two ways of getting the same number. Asked: the number.

Concept used: number =10x+y= 10x + y=10x+y (Topic 6); elimination. Why it applies: each "way" gives one equation.

  1. 1

    Let the tens digit be x and the units digit be y; take the difference as x−yx - yx−y (tens minus units).

  2. 2

    First way.

    10x+y=8(x+y)−510x + y = 8(x + y) - 510x+y=8(x+y)−5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Expand the bracket.

    10x+y=8x+8y−510x + y = 8x + 8y - 510x+y=8x+8y−5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract 8x8x8x from both sides.

    2x+y=8y−52x + y = 8y - 52x+y=8y−5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Subtract 8y8y8y from both sides.

    2x−7y=−5(1)2x - 7y = -5 \qquad (1)2x−7y=−5(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Second way.

    10x+y=16(x−y)+310x + y = 16(x - y) + 310x+y=16(x−y)+3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Expand the bracket.

    10x+y=16x−16y+310x + y = 16x - 16y + 310x+y=16x−16y+3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    Subtract 16x16x16x from both sides.

    −6x+y=−16y+3-6x + y = -16y + 3−6x+y=−16y+3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  9. 9

    Add 16y16y16y to both sides.

    −6x+17y=3-6x + 17y = 3−6x+17y=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  10. 10

    Multiply every term by −1-1−1.

    6x−17y=−3(2)6x - 17y = -3 \qquad (2)6x−17y=−3(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  11. 11

    Multiply every term of (1) by 3.

    6x−21y=−15(3)6x - 21y = -15 \qquad (3)6x−21y=−15(3)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  12. 12

    Subtract (3) from (2), term by term.

    (6x−6x)+(−17y+21y)=−3−(−15)(6x - 6x) + (-17y + 21y) = -3 - (-15)(6x−6x)+(−17y+21y)=−3−(−15)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  13. 13

    Simplify.

    4y=124y = 124y=12Swipe to see the whole equation →
  14. 14

    Divide by 4.

    y=3y = 3y=3Swipe to see the whole equation →
  15. 15

    Back-substitute into (1).

    2x−21=−52x - 21 = -52x−21=−5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  16. 16

    Add 21 to both sides.

    2x=162x = 162x=16Swipe to see the whole equation →
  17. 17

    Divide by 2.

    x=8x = 8x=8Swipe to see the whole equation →

  18. Check (story): the number is 83. 8×(8+3)−5=88−5=838 \times (8 + 3) - 5 = 88 - 5 = 838×(8+3)−5=88−5=83 ✔ and 16×(8−3)+3=80+3=8316 \times (8 - 3) + 3 = 80 + 3 = 8316×(8−3)+3=80+3=83 ✔. (Taking the difference as y−xy - xy−x gives a value of y that is not a whole number, so that case is rejected.)

  19. Answer The number is 83.

    Common trap: A sign slip in step 8 or 10 — for example writing 6x−17y=36x - 17y = 36x−17y=3 — gives y=92y = \dfrac{9}{2}y=29​, which is not a digit. A "digit" that is not a whole number from 0 to 9 is a signal to recheck the signs.

C1 — Case: a True/False test●● StandardCase/source-based · 4 marksCBSE Mathematics Class X Case Study Question Bank, Linear Equations in Two Variables, Case Study 1

A test consists of 'True' or 'False' questions. One mark is awarded for every correct answer while ¼ mark is deducted for every wrong answer. A student knew answers to some of the questions. Rest of the questions he attempted by guessing. He answered 120 questions and got 90 marks.

Type of Question Marks given for correct answer Marks deducted for wrong answer
True/False 1 0.25
  1. If answer to all questions he attempted by guessing were wrong, then how many questions did he answer correctly?
  2. How many questions did he guess?
  3. If answer to all questions he attempted by guessing were wrong and answered 80 correctly, then how many marks he got?
  4. If answer to all questions he attempted by guessing were wrong, then how many questions answered correctly to score 95 marks?

Full solution

Given: 120 questions answered; +1 for a correct answer, −14-\dfrac{1}{4}−41​ for a wrong one; 90 marks; every guess was wrong. Asked: four answers.

Concept used: a pair of linear equations from "number of questions" and "marks" (Topic 6). Why it applies: two facts, two unknowns.

  1. 1

    Let the number of questions he knew (all correct) be x and the number he guessed (all wrong) be y.

  2. 2

    Number of questions.

    x+y=120(1)x + y = 120 \qquad (1)x+y=120(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Marks: x−14y=90x - \dfrac{1}{4}y = 90x−41​y=90. Multiply every term by 4.

    4x−y=360(2)4x - y = 360 \qquad (2)4x−y=360(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Add (1) and (2).

    5x=4805x = 4805x=480Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Divide by 5: x=96x = 96x=96. Then from (1), y=24y = 24y=24.

  6. 6

    Part 1: 96 correct. Part 2: 24 guessed.

  7. 7

    Part 3: 80 correct means 120−80=40120 - 80 = 40120−80=40 wrong. Marks =80−14×40=80−10=70= 80 - \dfrac{1}{4} \times 40 = 80 - 10 = 70=80−41​×40=80−10=70.

  8. 8

    Part 4: with x correct, 120−x120 - x120−x are wrong: x−14(120−x)=95x - \dfrac{1}{4}(120 - x) = 95x−41​(120−x)=95. Multiply by 4: 4x−120+x=3804x - 120 + x = 3804x−120+x=380, so 5x=5005x = 5005x=500 and x=100x = 100x=100.

  9. Check: 96−244=96−6=9096 - \dfrac{24}{4} = 96 - 6 = 9096−424​=96−6=90 ✔; 100−204=95100 - \dfrac{20}{4} = 95100−420​=95 ✔.

  10. Answer

    1. 96 2. 24 3. 70 marks 4. 100 questions

    Common trap: In part 3, subtracting 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​ of 80 instead of 14\dfrac{1}{4}41​ of the 40 wrong answers.

C2 — Case: the layout of a house●● StandardCase/source-based · 5 marksCBSE Mathematics Class X Case Study Question Bank, Linear Equations in Two Variables, Case Study 2

Amit is planning to buy a house and the layout is given below. The design and the measurement has been made such that areas of two bedrooms and kitchen together is 95 sq.m.

(Picture, described: a rectangle 15 m long. The top strip, 5 m high, holds Bedroom 1 (width x m), a bathroom (width 2 m) and the kitchen (width y m), side by side, so x+2+y=15x + 2 + y = 15x+2+y=15. Below it is a 2 m wide passage that is part of the living room. The bottom strip, 5 m high, holds Bedroom 2 (width x m) on the left, with the rest of the living room to its right. The total height is 5+2+5=125 + 2 + 5 = 125+2+5=12 m.)

  1. Form the pair of linear equations in two variables from this situation.
  2. Find the length of the outer boundary of the layout.
  3. Find the area of each bedroom and kitchen in the layout.
  4. Find the area of living room in the layout.
  5. Find the cost of laying tiles in kitchen at the rate of Rs. 50 per sq.m

Full solution

Given: the layout and the total area of the two bedrooms and the kitchen. Asked: five answers.

Concept used: areas of rectangles; a pair of linear equations (Topic 6). Why it applies: the widths x and y are unknown.

  1. 1

    Each bedroom is 5×x=5x5 \times x = 5x5×x=5x m² and the kitchen is 5y5y5y m²: 5x+5x+5y=955x + 5x + 5y = 955x+5x+5y=95, that is 10x+5y=9510x + 5y = 9510x+5y=95, or

    2x+y=19(1)2x + y = 19 \qquad (1)2x+y=19(1)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    The top strip: x+2+y=15x + 2 + y = 15x+2+y=15, that is

    x+y=13(2)x + y = 13 \qquad (2)x+y=13(2)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Subtract (2) from (1): x=6x = 6x=6. Then y=7y = 7y=7.

  4. 4

    Part 2: the outer boundary is a 15 m by 12 m rectangle: 2(15+12)=542(15 + 12) = 542(15+12)=54 m.

  5. 5

    Part 3: each bedroom 5×6=305 \times 6 = 305×6=30 m²; kitchen 5×7=355 \times 7 = 355×7=35 m².

  6. 6

    Part 4: the living room is the 2 m passage (15×2=3015 \times 2 = 3015×2=30 m²) plus the part beside Bedroom 2 (5×(15−6)=455 \times (15 - 6) = 455×(15−6)=45 m²): 757575 m². (Equivalently, the bottom 7 m of the house, 15×7=10515 \times 7 = 10515×7=105 m², minus Bedroom 2, 30 m².)

  7. 7

    Part 5: 35×50=175035 \times 50 = 175035×50=1750.

  8. Check: 30+30+35=9530 + 30 + 35 = 9530+30+35=95 m² ✔; 6+2+7=156 + 2 + 7 = 156+2+7=15 m ✔.

  9. Answer

    1. 2x+y=192x + y = 192x+y=19 and x+y=13x + y = 13x+y=13 2. 54 m 3. bedrooms 30 m² each, kitchen 35 m² 4. 75 m² 5. ₹ 1750

    Common trap: Counting only one bedroom in the area equation. "Two bedrooms and kitchen" gives 5x+5x+5y5x + 5x + 5y5x+5x+5y.
    Note

    the bank's printed answer writes the bedroom and kitchen areas as "30m" and "35m"; they are areas, in square metres.

C3 — Case: auto fares in two cities● FoundationCase/source-based · 3 marksCBSE Mathematics Class X Case Study Question Bank, Linear Equations in Two Variables, Case Study 3 (parts 1–3)

It is common that Governments revise travel fares from time to time based on various factors such as inflation (a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money) on different types of vehicles like auto, Rickshaws, taxis, Radio cab etc. The auto charges in a city comprise of a fixed charge together with the charge for the distance covered. Study the following situations.

(Pictures: an auto-rickshaw and a taxi.)

Name of the city Distance travelled (Km) Amount paid (Rs.)
City A 10 75
15 110
City B 8 91
14 145

Situation 1: In city A, for a journey of 10 km, the charge paid is Rs 75 and for a journey of 15 km, the charge paid is Rs 110.
Situation 2: In a city B, for a journey of 8km, the charge paid is Rs91 and for a journey of 14km, the charge paid is Rs 145.

Refer situation 1

  1. If the fixed charges of auto rickshaw be Rs x and the running charges be Rs y km/hr, the pair of linear equations representing the situation is (a) x+10y=110x + 10y = 110x+10y=110, x+15y=75x + 15y = 75x+15y=75 (b) x+10y=75x + 10y = 75x+10y=75, x+15y=110x + 15y = 110x+15y=110 (c) 10x+y=11010x + y = 11010x+y=110, 15x+y=7515x + y = 7515x+y=75 (d) 10x+y=7510x + y = 7510x+y=75, 15x+y=11015x + y = 11015x+y=110
  2. A person travels a distance of 50km. The amount he has to pay is (a) Rs.155 (b) Rs.255 (c) Rs.355 (d) Rs.455

Refer situation 2

  1. What will a person have to pay for travelling a distance of 30km? (a) Rs.185 (b) Rs.289 (c) Rs.275 (d) Rs.305

Full solution

Given: two journeys in each city. Asked: three answers.

Concept used: total = fixed charge + (charge per km) × distance (Topic 6). Why it applies: the fixed charge is the same for both journeys in a city.

  1. 1

    City A: x+10y=75x + 10y = 75x+10y=75 and x+15y=110x + 15y = 110x+15y=110 → (b).

  2. 2

    Subtract: 5y=355y = 355y=35, so y=7y = 7y=7 and x=75−70=5x = 75 - 70 = 5x=75−70=5. For 50 km: 5+50×7=3555 + 50 \times 7 = 3555+50×7=355 → (c).

  3. 3

    City B: x+8y=91x + 8y = 91x+8y=91 and x+14y=145x + 14y = 145x+14y=145. Subtract: 6y=546y = 546y=54, so y=9y = 9y=9 and x=91−72=19x = 91 - 72 = 19x=91−72=19. For 30 km: 19+30×9=28919 + 30 \times 9 = 28919+30×9=289 → (b).

  4. Check: City A: 5+15×7=1105 + 15 \times 7 = 1105+15×7=110 ✔. City B: 19+14×9=14519 + 14 \times 9 = 14519+14×9=145 ✔.

  5. Answer 1 (b) · 2 (c) · 3 (b)

    Common trap: In part 1, choosing (d) — putting the distance with the fixed charge x instead of with the rate y.
    Notes on the bank's wording

    Part 1 says "Rs y km/hr"; it means ₹ y per km (a charge, not a speed). The bank's part 4 asks which of four printed graphs shows Situation 2; none of them does — the graph marked as the answer uses a line from City A — so that part is left out here.
